TFT Opener Guide Set 17

Patch 17.5a has a lot of different win cons in each tier. Xayah has an extremely high cap and is likely to win most lobbies. Fast 9 is a close second for the highest cap in the game.
Guide will be updated every patch

Table of Contents
Broken Openers:
Augments
How to find and decide on an Opener
Items
Checklist for considering a win streak opener
Comps to play from win streak
Unit Priority Stage 1
1 Costs
2 Costs
3 Costs
How to Lose Streak
Lose Streak Comeback Mechanic
Generic Openers
Flex
Generic AD
Generic AP
Broken Openers:
Verticals/Hard Force:Stargazer Xayah
Conditional:Emblems Augment -> Space Groove, Dark Stars, Brawler Yi
8+ Winstreak? -> Vex Fast 9, Vanguard Fast 9
Anima Cash Out -> Stargazer Xayah, Mecha
Artifacts -> Mecha, Brawler Yi, Lulu Reroll, Stargazer Xayah
Gnar + Slam -> Gnar Printer
Reroll Check:Stargazer opener? -> Lulu Reroll
Treasure Hunt -> Lulu Reroll
Lose Streak:Always play Timebreakers or Primordians if offered
Play for a strong stage 4 comp like Stargazer Xayah, Corki Riven
Click a strong directional augment on 3-2 if availableThings like Emblems, Artifacts or other random output augments that enable win out set ups
Although this patch is predominantly AD focused, there still are a wide variety of lines available. AP can be played from high tempo spots but is often hard to justify from loss streak due to reliance on 2 star 5 costs.
Augments
Expedition
Full open while feeding 3 gold worth of units to the hex each turn. Aim to cash out by 4-1. Radiant Nashor’s performs very well so consider Dark Star Lissandra or Lulu Reroll. Mecha with Radiant Gargoyle’s is also great.
Prismatic Ticket
Look to play Lulu Reroll or another reroll comp reliant on hitting multiple 3 stars.
Branching Out/Spreading Roots/Legion of Threes/Trait Tree
Take these and allow the game to give you strong direction. Avoid them if you already have a very solid direction you rather play into. Avoid if you already have a strong a strong direction. Ex: TF 2 with a Jax in a good Stargazer constellation.
Portable Forge/Living Forge
Data check your artifacts and hard force any interaction that averages 4.5 or better.
Worth the Wait I
Veigar is very stable early mid game and opens up playing for Veigar 4 in the Veigar Meeple composition.
Finding Lissandra 3 without having to roll is very powerful as she can be main carried the entire game.
Ezreal and Cho infinitely scale but without a slam can often be a bit too slow.
Anything in B tier will be good for a top 4 but if you get to 9 will likely not be part of a fully capped board.
C and F tier is the stuff you don’t want to see.

Worth the Wait II
Just like 1 cost this augment is pretty consistent. It’s not as good as the power level of Prismatics is much higher than golds, but it is still a great augment.
Millio 3 deals a lot of damage and is an easy slot in for Corki Riven and Lulu Reroll
Gwen is very likely to win streak you and will remain strong later on into the game, just make sure you keep 2 Rogue in.
Pantheon is a premiere front liner that solves your front line for the rest of the game.
Gnar 4 can be achieved earlier by using the 7 Meeple printing hex.
Morde and Meepsie are great 3 trait flex units you don’t mind having 3 starred a lot of the time.
Pyke is S if you have Target-Lock Optics as a Psionic item in the early game.

U.R.F./URF’s Gambit
Emblems are currently very strong and these augments should be prioritized heavily. Prioritize Darkstar Emblem.
Anima Commander
Full open, if you win a fight you are down an augment. It’s kind of hard to take this augment if your lobby is weak and playing into time breakers. If you lose your loss streak you are in a bad spot. Getting extra HP also makes it hard to be in the bottom 2 for reforgers and item anvils.
Calculated Loss
Full open and look play a 3 cost reroll line. Lulu Reroll and Urgot Reroll are ideal.
Two Tanky
Play Two Tanky Samira.
No Scout No Pivot
Consider Dark Star Lissandra, make sure Lissandra is fielded after Cho’Gath to ensure she is the super massive.
Early Learnings
Play any 1 cost reroll comp, ideally Leona Teemo or TF but Ezreal Cho’Gath works as well. Your cap is very high if you reroll 1 costs with this augment.
Solo Plate
This augment is very broken and BIS on Leona and Mecha.
If you don’t have direction at all augments such as Expected Unexpectedness and Birthday Reunion provide units to begin playing around.
Econ Augments:Econ from augments can come in the form of raw gold, units, rerolls, or EXP. Each resource interacts with your spot in different ways and have distinct advantages from each other.
Raw gold is best when your goal is to loss streak and make interest intervals quickly. Consider augments like Savings Account, Calculated Loss and Cognitive Tax when you want to focus on making econ.
Units provide tempo, if you take an augment that gives you units you should be looking to be decently strong, specially if it provides star levels. Consider augments like Kick Start, Booster Pack, Warpath, and Birthday Reunion to turn a somewhat strong opener, into a very strong opener.
Rerolls can be used immediately if you already have a lot of pairs and can provide a meaningful spike in the early game. Take these when looking to complete pairs or trait break points for things like Timebreaker and Primordian. Consider augments like Trade Sector, Patience is a Virtue and
EXP is by default going to make you stronger than your opponents as you will be higher level. This almost always leads to some sort of level 8 or 9 strategy where you try to capitalize on the fact that you are naturally over leveled. Take these type of augments when you want to level quickly. Consider Epoch, Level Up and Silver Spoon if you want to get ahead of the lobby’s curve.
How to find and decide on an Opener
The highest priority when choosing an opener is solid direction. Choosing a solid gameplan early and committing to it confidently. If you see a strong reroll augment, don’t be afraid to commit. If you see an artifact that boosts a comp up a tier, be willing to commit and play a simple but efficient game of TFT.
All tier lists below are focused on how easy it is to 5 win streak with these units, they do not take into account what line they lead down.
Items

Burn and utility items are very important in this meta and are also decent early game slams. Sword is the best component in this meta as it is very heavy towards AD. Both Xayah and Yi’s traits don’t provide a whole lot of base stats so items like Deathblade perform very well on both these units. Bows are also a high priority due to Kraken Slayer and Red Buff’s strength. If you have to make AP items avoid itemes like Shojin as the best AP unit at the moment is Asol who does not want mana generation items. If you do make mana generation items look to end in some comp that itemizes Sona.
Win Streak
If you can win streak while taking an econ augment or 2 look to go level 9 as Vex is one of the highest caps in the game at the moment. Level 8 lines are much easier to play from win streak as you have HP and are able to go 9 to transition to legendaries or play for a 3 star 4 cost. Overall if you can win streak you are less constricted in the lines you can successfully play to a top 4.
If you have a special condition play into that.
Your options are incredibly open from win streak.
Most level 8 lines can cap out decently high on level 9 if you are forced to roll on 8.
When you are playing for a win streak look to complete items on the Gods round aggressively. When you slam an item consider what components you will be left with because you want to be able to continue building items to maintain your win streak. You are likely not going to get your desired items so build items that fulfill similar roles. Ex: Deathblade instead of Kraken even if you might prefer Kraken as they both fulfill the role of providing AD.
Checklist for considering a win streak opener
A strong item slam on a 2 star unit
Upgrades
A item or combat augment
Thorough scouting of the lobby to ensure it is realistic to win streak for 3+ rounds
Comps to play from win streak
Brawler Yi, Vex Fast 9, Asol Flex, Stargazer Xayah, Gnar Printer
Unit Priority Stage 1
1 Costs

2 Rogue remains the strongest early game trait due to the high base stats and aggro drop. Slam AD items on either one and look to play Yi or Xayah. Prim and Brawler are great early game traits so Rek’Sai is S tier. Lissandra when paired with a Pantheon can make for an above average AP spot that leads into Asol. Vanguards are quite strong in the early game. Lower tier units are more conditional to get online. Units like Caitlyn can start to look better if you have specific items for them like a Guinsoo’s.
2 Costs

Pantheon and Millio are strong as is 2 Timebreaker. Bel’Veth herself is not great but Primordian is a great early game trait. Psionic items are more generically useful and provide value regardless of if you’re AD or AP. Pyke was already a great unit in the early game but with the buffs to Psionic he is now amazing. Jinx has been buffed thoroughly and is very strong with 2 Challenger. All of the B tier units are playable within the right context or traits, they’re about equal in power. Akali is not very strong but her NOVA buff can be useful later in the game.
3 Costs

Illaoi is one of the tankiest units in stage 2 and can often lead to a 5 streak. MF is decent in all of her forms but Challenger MF is very strong without traits and an absolute demon with 2 Challenger. Kai’Sa is a great unit that will carry stage 2 and 3 consistently. The fact that she’s a Rogue also means she synergizes with other S tier holds. She also opens up 4 Dark Star which is a really high tempo mid game, hold her every time you see her. The B tier units can be ok if you have traits for them but not very high priority and can be sold to hold lower cost pairs. If you happen to have 2 upgraded backliners and no front line, Rhaast can be an ok hold in the early game, otherwise sell him.
Lose Streak
Checklist for considering a loss streak opener
No/weak direction
No or low upgrade count
An econ augment
Econ Gods are preferred.
How to Lose Streak

Loss streak is not great at the moment. Timebreaker got nerfed to require 3 units and Anima is only good if you can cash out 400 which requires having it on 2-1.
The only 2 reliable game plans from a weak opener are to either take an econ augment on 2-1 or having some sort of condition that allows you to hard stabilize on stage 4 and play for a win out. There are not a lot of reroll lines at the moment so only consider them if you have a special condition for them. Ex: Radiant Nashor’s into Lulu Reroll or Dark Star Lissandra
Primordian is the worst econ trait in terms of gold value but is by no means bad. Primordian gives it value in the form of units which can be tempo. By playing this trait with a few lucky generated units you can put together a strong enough board to start winning fights in stage 3.
If you end up winning and snapping your loss streak. Don’t full open from this point. Keep playing your econ trait but otherwise play strongest and look to kill units or beat other people opening. If you can’t keep the loss streak look to save HP instead.
If you are heavily loss streaking and you are not playing to spike very hard on stage 4 you are likely to bot 4. Most of the time if you are loss streaking and you don’t have a special condition such as an emblem, it is advised to contest Corki Riven or Master Yi if you have to due to their strength through stage 4 and early 5. It is often better to flip your game with econ augments and try to hit Corki 2 and Rammus 2 on 4-1 as opposed to playing an uncontested line. Playing AP from loss streak is almost always a recipe for disaster due to tough match ups against Corki Riven and Master Yi players.
Lose Streak Comeback Mechanic
When playing loss streak your main advantage is a hidden comeback mechanic of getting anvils on neutral rounds instead of random components. Your top priority is item quality. There is no need to slam subpar items if you know you are likely to lose fights anyway. Look to greed BIS so you can spike hard on stage 3 around a reroll carry.
Generic Openers
These sample boards are generically strong and can be flexed into different lines depending on your augments.
Flex
These boards can carry both an AD or AP carry easily. There are a lot of comps with duo carries in the meta at the moment so these flex boards hold for duo carry set ups extremely well.

This board can go directly into Lulu Reroll if you natural enough copies in a good Stargazer and are uncontested. If you choose to level it can play into any level 8 line or Vex Fast 9 if you win streak for long enough. If you have the Boar Stargazer and win most of stage 3 take augments to go fast 9 as you will be very rich.
Comps to play:
Lulu Reroll, Vex Fast 9, Brawler Yi, Asol Flex, Corki Riven, Stargazer Xayah, Gnar Printer
2 Rogue + Front

Gwen with 2 Rogue is very consistent at win streaking. She has a lot of damage and is very safe compared to full melee rogues and has a lot of scam potential. Almost any slam is good in this opener as Talon can hold almost any AD items and Gwen can hold any AP items. Overall a premium win streak opener due to how strong Gwen is early game.
Comps to play:
Vex Fast 9, Corki Riven, Asol Flex, Brawler Yi, Stargazer Xayah
Timebreaker Fateweaver

A weaker opener around Timebreakers to build econ but still has access to flexible carries that can hold any item you might want to slam. Look to spike hard on stage 4 if you are too weak early on into the game.
Comps to play:
Lulu Reroll, Vex Fast 9, Brawler Yi, Asol Flex, Corki Riven, Stargazer Xayah
Generic AD
Gnar Meeple

Gnar is a great user of Guinsoo’s and can win streak you into fast 9 or Brawler Yi.
Consider Xayah if the Stargazer is good.
Comps to play:
Jhin Fast 9, Vex Fast 9, Stargazer Xayah, Corki Riven, Brawler Yi, Gnar Printer
Primordian

Win streak opener around Bel’Veth and Akali holding AD items. Great if you have Brawler or Marauder emblem. Most of the time you will play into Brawler Yi from decent HP from this opener on this patch. If you win for long enough you can play for a Fast 9.
Comps to play:
Brawler Yi, Vex Fast 9, Jhin Fast 9
Timebreaker Snipers

Loss streak AD is not recommended. Gnar and Ezreal have good single target and will get a decent amount of kills however. Look to play Corki Riven or into some sort of special condition. Xayah in a combat Stargazer can be considered. If you are loss streaking play into Corki Riven.
Comps to play:
Brawler Yi, Dark Stars, Corki Riven, Gnar Printer, Stargazer Xayah
Generic AP
3 Shepherd Lissandra

The core for this set up is 3 Shepherd. Play 2 Replicator if you have it, ideally with Pantheon. Lissandra is one of the few 1 cost that dodged nerfs this patch so she holds AP items very efficiently. Don’t make mana items if you are planning on playing Asol.
Comps to play:
Asol Flex, Vanguard Karma Leblanc, 7 Shepherd, Vex Fast 9,
Zoe Leona

Opener to play when Arbiter is good. If you are not planning on playing LeBlanc or a a line that keeps Leona, prioritize econ Arbiters. Otherwise look for Arbiters gain max HP on 50 Mana spent to make a huge Leona or anything that produces copies of Leona to cheat out Leona 3. Zoe is very strong and holds Asol items very efficiently because they both dislike mana items

Comps to play:
Asol Flex, Vanguard Karma Leblanc, 7 Shepherd, Vex Fast 9

Best TFT Builds & Team Comps for Set 17 Patch 17.5b Meta
S: Stargazer Xayah, Gnar Printer, Two Tanky Samira Reroll, Vex Fast 9,
A: Brawler Yi, Vanguard Fast 9, Space Groove, Dark Stars, Mecha, Primordian Jinx
B: Corki Riven, Lissandra Reroll, Vanguard Karma Leblanc, 7 Shepherd, Miss Fortune Reroll, Jhin Fast 9, Shepherd Viktor, Lulu Reroll,
C: NOVA Marauders, Urgot Reroll, Twisted Fate Reroll, Meeple Veigar, Cho’Gath Ezreal Reroll, Leona Teemo Reroll,Rogue Reroll, Primordian Reroll,
Very Special: Self Destruct Gragas, Big Bang Meepsie,
Special: Invader Zed, Reach For The Stars Jax, Shieldmaiden Leona, Termeepnal Velocity, Stellar Combo Aatrox,
Not Special: Bonk! Nasus, Heat Death Mordekaiser, Contract Killer Pyke,
Comps to 1 trick: Stargazer Xayah,
Exodia Comps: Vex Fast 9, Two Tanky Samira Reroll,
Beginner Comps (Below Diamond): Lissandra Reroll,
* = has a big requirement such as an emblem or specific augment
Special Tier = Requires a specific setup to work (Note that “Not Special” doesn’t mean never click, it just means it’s worse than the other special tiers)

Note that Items don’t really matter that much, so don’t grief your game to get specific items unless I mention a specific item is required.
Try out different types of positioning and champions in these TFT builds too! There is a ton of variation in TFT so be sure to check out the Core units in the tierlist and then flex the rest of your team!

Conditions:
Tempo AD Opener
Serpent, Boar, or Altar Stargazer constellation
Lots of Bows
How to Play:
Gameplan: Standard fast 8 comp. If you don’t have Serpent, Boar, or Altar Stargazer constellation play something else. Xayah is very BIS dependent and wants Red Buff and Krakens so prioritize item augments. Rhaast is very important to this comp, prioritize playing traits on level 8 to provide you without enough strength to go level 9.Stage 1-2: Play a strong AD opener around Kraken or Guinsoo’s slam. This comp is playable from loss streak due to the hefty bow requirement but aim to be strong around an attack speed slam such as Red, Guinsoo’s or Kraken if available.
Stage 3: Keep up tempo and collect BIS Xayah, if you have more swords than bows, hold Meeples and look to pivot to Corki.
Stage 4: Roll down for Xayah 2 and a 2 star 4 cost tank, either Tahm Kench, Nunu or Rammus will do. If you are tanking Rammus, 3 Meeple is mandatory. The TK Nunu variant is easier to flex around than Rammus variant due to 3 Meeple being required.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 when possible and look for Jhin 2. The best in at 9 most of the time will be Blitzcrank.
Tips:
Xayah’s items are really specific, play something else if you don’t have at least 1 Kraken and premium AS item like Guinsoo’s or Red Buff.
Any augment that allows you to access Radiant Red Buff is a great option. Consider Expedition and Golden Gamble heavily.
Jhin needs Infinity Edge and heavy AD items, do not get baited into making a Guinsoo’s for him.
Titanic Hydra is insanely OP on Xayah and you should hard force her if you see this artifact.
Nunu wants mana items, TK wants raw tank items. Making a random Vow for Nunu + 3 other tank items for TK is perfectly fine in this comp.
Don’t build Sunder due to the fact that this board almost always runs Aatrox.
Serpent > Boar > Altar > 2-1 Mountain > Fountain > Huntress > Medallion
The latest you are allowed to play Mountain Stargazer on your board is 2-3 to have a consistent game.
Item Holder: Gnar, Caitlyn

Jhin: Infinity Edge, Last Whisper, Striker’s
Rammus: Generic Tank
Bard: Archangel’s, Morello, Void Staff
Gods: Ahri, Kayle

General: Items > Econ > Combat

Conditions:
Meeple +1 makes printing easier
Lots of Swords
Enough HP to print Gnar
Gods: Varus, Kayle, Yasuo
How to Play:
Gameplan: Play around a strong 3 Meeple + Gnar Opener with a strong slam. This is a tempo comp as you will need enough HP to print Gnar utilizing 7 Meeple. This is not a reroll comp, you will not be staying down on level 6 and slowrolling for Gnar.Stage 1-2: Play your strongest board around Gnar, 3 Meeple and a slam. If you aren’t strong and able to save HP, consider a different line.
Stage 3: Consider rolling on 3-2 to stabilize around Gnar 2 or find Econ traits such as Timebreakers. Make sure to not roll down too aggressively as you will need money to hit 7 Meeple on Stage 4.
Stage 4: Level to 8 as soon as possible for 7 Meeple. Stabilize around Rammus 2 and Corki 2. If you’ve taken item augments you should be able to play around 3 item Gnar and Corki.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 when possible for Jhin + Karma. If you made to Gnar 3 + Jhin you are likely to top 4.
Tips:
Every time you print a copy you will get gold. Don’t be afraid to dig aggressively on stage 4 for upgrades as you will make your money back through printing Gnar 3.
The more HP you save early on or even while printing Gnar, the better the game is likely to go. The easiest way to do poorly with this comp is if you didn’t give yourself enough time to successfully print Gnar 3.
Heavily prioritize item augments.

Conditions:
S Tier with Two Tanky
Lots of Swords
Lots of Econ
Samira drop
Gods: Varus, Ahri, Kayle
How to Play:
Gameplan: Play this from a strong Space Groove opener, ideally a Samira orb from neutrals. This comp requires a lot of swords as Samira is very BIS dependent. If you are able to reach Samira 3, Ornn 3 and 7 Space Groove you have a great chance at winning the game. If you have Two Tanky you have great odds at winning the game if you get there.Stage 1-2: Play your strongest opener around a Samira slam and look to save HP. If you don’t have an opener look to loss streak and econ up for a 3-5 all in.
Stage 3: Look to stabilize around 3-5 if necessary with Samira and 5 Space Groove.
Stage 4: Continue to roll for your 3 star upgrades. Be as strong as possible early stage 4 as level 9 players will beat you before you hit 3 stars.
Stage 5+: Level for Space Groove units after 3 starring Ornn and Samira. If you reach 7 Space Groove you will be in contention for top 2.
Tips:
5 Space Groove is the most important trait break point as it provides units AP/AD per second spent in the Groove.
Samira performs much worse without BIS so heavily prioritize augments that allow you to find it.
If you have Two Tanky your board will always consist of 2 Ornns, 2 Samiras and 5+ Space Groove. Level 8 is Bastion or a 6th Groove unit. Level 9 is always 7 Groove once you find Blitzcrank.
Infinity Edge is bugged on Samira so avoid building it in this line.

Conditions:
Ability to get to level 9 comfortably
3 Item Vex, 3 Item secondary carry and 3 item tank
Can be pivoted into from LeBlanc lines
How to Play:
Gameplan: Fast 9 is rough this set as there is no 5 cost tank to stabilize your front line, meaning often times if you can’t fast 9 by 4-5 all the copies of front liners will be gone. Most of the time you will pivot into this board from a level 8 comp as skipping 8 can be risky at the moment. Vex is the strongest cap at the moment. Graves also caps very high but is hard to play into if you get him after 5-2, the earlier the better.Stage 1-2: Play your strongest opener and look to win streak. If you aren’t winning you will likely need to pivot to a different comp. Take econ augments and build a gold lead.
Stage 3: Continue to be strong, the longer you sustain your win streak the easier the game will be. Considering pivoting to LeBlanc if you’ve slammed Vex items and can’t keep up the win streak.
Stage 4: If you can go 9 on 4-5, do so to find a 4 cost 2 star tank. The earlier you find Graves the better. Vex 1 + a 2 star 4 cost tank should be stable for the rest of stage 4.
Stage 5+: Go 9 if you haven’t already and roll for your board. The latest turn Graves is playable is 5-2. If you can’t find Graves add front line for Vex.
Tips:
Graves Build path: Assault Frame > Buckshot > Buckshot+ > Buckshot++ > Laser Ballistics. Assault Frame is the best initial choice. Go for a tanky Graves if you don’t have good items for him.
Prioritize CC immunity on Graves.
This comp can be pivoted in to from LeBlanc variants as LB and Vex share the same itemization.
Shred/Sunder and Spell Crit aren’t necessary as Akali’s and Aatrox’s NOVA buff offers it after 6 seconds of combat.
Item Holder: Talon, Gwen
Items:
Vex: Guinsoo’s, Giant Slayer, GunbladeAny AP slammed for tempo is fine, avoid Shojin

Nunu: Protector’s Vow/Mana generating Tank items

BIS: Misfits
General: Econ > Item > Combat > Trait

Conditions:
AD Psionic item is preferred but not required
Loves Emblem Augments
Gods: Kayle, Ahri
How to Play:
Gameplan: This comp is the best user of Emblems at the moment due to the amount of hanging traits. Yi can utilize many emblems and these can serve as his itemization. Prioritize Edge of Night as aggro drop is key to keeping Yi alive. This comp is best played from tempo and should not be leaned into from loss streak.Stage 1-2: Check your Psionic as soon as possible and look to commit if you have an AD item. Play your strongest AD opener while slamming Yi and Kindred items. Pyke is a great item holder to streak through stage 2, but will fall off in stage 3. Primordian is a strong option that can also provide extra econ.
Stage 3: Continue to play your strongest board and collecting Yi items. Your holds will be different depending on if you played this from an Emblem Augment.
Stage 4: Roll down on 4-2 for Yi, Kindred and TK. Flex around whatever emblems you have available to you if you clicked an emblem augment. If you don’t have any extra emblems prioritize 4 Brawler and 4 Marauder as these are cheap traits that stabilize your board consistently on stage 4.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 as soon as possible and look for Fiora and other 5 cost.
Tips:
Since Yi is a melee carry aura buffs such as Morgana’s Dark Lady and Shen’s Bulwark are incredibly useful as they keep him alive much more consistently.
Kindred holds Target Lock Optics better than Yi does.
Malware Matrix is by far the best Psionic item on Yi as it helps him shred through front lines faster.
Emblem Priority: Marauder > Brawler > Psionic = Challenger > NOVA
Max cap is Fiora and Vex 2.

Conditions:
Space Groove +1 for Riven makes this much better
How to Play:
Gameplan: Space Groove is best played if you have access to an emblem. Riven synergizes incredibly well with Space Groove’s healing and stacking AD/AP as she will almost always be in the Groove due to the small mana pool. Many augments offer access to spats or emblems so finding +1 Space Groove is realistic. If you don’t have access to Space Groove emblem this comp is a complete Blitzcrank check as 7 Space Groove is over stated.Stage 1-2: Play your strongest Space Groove opener. Gwen + Talon is a great opener, specially if you have Space Groove +1 for Talon. If you don’t have an emblem yet don’t commit to this line yet.
Stage 3: Continue picking up Space Groove units, if you find a spat on 3-2, commit. If your board naturally leads into 7 Space Groove and you have enough HP to consistently reach level 9 for Blitzcrank, you can also consider committing to this line.
Stage 4: Roll aggressively on 4-2 for Riven 2, Nami 2 and a 2 star front liner. If you find Blitz on 8 you are very likely to be in a good spot, if you don’t play Nasus in his place.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 when possible and play 7 Space Groove.
Tips:
If you don’t have a Space Groove +1 force this line.
5 Space Groove is the most important trait break point as it provides units AP/AD per second spent in the Groove.
Nunu, Ornn or TK can be main tanked but ideally it’s Nunu with multiple Vows to CC the enemy board.
Prioritize CC immunity on Riven with Space Groove Emblem to maximize uptime.

Conditions:
Dark Star Emblem
Item Augments
Gods: Kayle, Ahri
How to Play:
Gameplan: Look to play this primarily off Dark Star Emblem. This comp loves emblems and has multiple variants. There are 3 main Dark Star Emblem lines being Riven, Asol and Xayah. You will often decide which is best to play based on other emblems you might have or whatever you slam in the early game.Stage 1-2: Play around a trait augment such as Trait tree and look to play 4 Dark Star as soon as possible due to its high stats. Slam Riven, Asol or Xayah items on a carry and try to be strong around extra stats provided by emblem augments.
Stage 3: Continue being strong by adding Dark Star units and whatever front line you’ve upgraded. Be flexible and play around hanging traits.
Stage 4: Level to 8 on 4-2 and look to spike around 6 Dark Star and 2 star 4 cost. All variants are very stable on level 8.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 when possible. Jhin is the highest cap and should be played as soon as possible.
Tips:
Dark Star already gives a high amount of AD/AP so pair the emblem with items that provide different stats. Riven wants items that provide survivability such as Sterak’s and HoJ, while Xayah wants attack speed. Asol wants crit and damage amp from items like Jeweled Gauntlet and Striker’s. Avoid building items that give raw stats playing this line and prioritize other multipliers from the items you build.
6 Dark Star is playable without an emblem but you need to have guaranteed access to Jhin. If you have something like Aura Farming Jhin, consider this line heavily.
Avoid scaling items in this line as you already have so much up front value from Dark Star AD and AP.
Item Holder: Talon, Briar, Gwen, Ezreal
Best Emblem/Spatula Holder: Dark Star Riven, Dark Star Xayah, Dark Star Asol

Conditions:
3 Item Asol and Mech by 4-2
BIS Mech
How to Play:
Gameplan: The easiest way to do well with this comp is to have some sort of special item. Either a Radiant, Artifact or Anima item on Asol or Mech can significantly boost your placement.Stage 1-2: Collect Mech BIS and econ up to make sure you can find Mech and Asol by 4-2.
Stage 3: Save as much HP as possible while collecting your items. If you don’t have access to any special items and find a better direction consider pivoting.
Stage 4: Level to 8 on 4-2, 4-1 if you are low HP and roll for Mech 2 and Asol 2. These 2 units with 6 Mech in are overstated and will stabilize your stage 4 and early 5. The sooner you find a TK the sooner you will start scaling. If you are too low prioritize playing strongest over TK.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 when possible and play any 5 cost you find. This comp never goes 9 before having Mech 2 and Asol 2.
Tips:
BIS Mech is required, item quality is everything in this comp. Never drop Gargoyle’s.
Asol in Mecha form does not auto attack, making items like Shojin and Nashor’s completely worthless.
Ekko’s offerings are good to loss streak with and his Boon performs very well on Asol.
Yasuo Power Hexes are strong in this comp as your board is almost all Mech and Asol. Cryogenic is the best for Mech and Storm Hex for Asol. Power hexes act as 4th items on these 2 slot hyper carries.
If you are contested always play TK to print copies, hitting your 2 stars is too important.
Akali and Maokai are great supportive units on level 8 with Akali giving Asol free spell crit but are not highest cap.
Urgot can take any random AD items you might have and utilize them quite well. Consider Urgot 3 if no one is holding copies and you find AD artifacts from augments like Living Forge and Forged in Strength.

Conditions:
Item augments
Early copies
High tempo
Gods:
How to Play:
Gameplan: Play this comp from high tempo and item augments. If you are able to reach 3 item Jinx, Bel’Veth and Akali you are in a great spot for a top 2. This is the type of comp you natural into stage 2, not something you force without copies.Stage 1-2: Play around early Jinx and Primordians. Slam items to keep tempo.
Stage 3: Roll on 3-2 and stabilize. Look to be strong on this stage as Jinx 2 plus upgrades will beat most stage 3 boards.
Stage 4: Continue to roll for 3 stars and ideally hit by 4-5. Look to level for Rhaast as soon as possible. Consider dropping Briar if you are too low HP.
Stage 5+: Continue leveling when possible and adding Challenger units or legendaries. This comp doesn’t cap the highest but can be good for a top 2 if you have sufficient tempo from stage 3, 4 and early 5.
Tips:
Item Prio: Jinx > Bel’Veth > Akali > Tank
Prioritize pure damage items on Jinx. Jinx has access to enough attack speed from Challenger to let her cast reliably, and a multiplier from Precision granted by Akali’s NOVA buff, meaning that raw AD is the most efficient stat on Jinx because it’s what she lacks. Do not build Shojin on Jinx.
Play Briar for econ during stage 3 and early 4 but look to drop out of her for Rhaast at level 7 after hitting your board. You can add her back in at 8 if you don’t have a better in.
Emblems are very solid in this comp and should be heavily considered.
Kill chains, tears and rods on tank items for Rek’Sai.
This comp ideally doesn’t take econ augments unless they provide a lot of tempo at 2-1.
Item Holder: Jinx, Bel’Veth, Akali, Briar, Rek’Sai

Corki can already crit as he’s a Fateweaver so prioritize items that give crit chance.

Never Mech Asol.Stage 1-2: Play your strongest AP opener with ideally an emblem or item augment. This comp can utilize almost every AP slam as you should aim to have 3 Asol items plus another 3 item carry by late game.
Stage 3: Continue to be strong if possible during this stage. Make sure to hold lower cost units you can flex in like Lissandra and Meepsie during these turns.
Stage 4: Level on 4-2 and look for Asol, a duo carry and front line. Roll aggressively here before copies of front line 4 cost are all gone.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 and look to replace lower value units for legendaries. Ideally cap around Bard, Sona and Blitzcrank.

Duo carry priority: Sona 2 > Karma 2 > Nami 2 > Sona 1LeBlanc can be played but is much more specific (requires Rageblade)

If you have Dark Star Emblem play 6 Dark Star Asol.
Vanguard, Voyager and Shepherd emblems are great conditions for this comp.
Asol wants full damage, don’t build mana items.
Nunu prefers casting items like Vow while Mighty Mech prefers pure tank items like Gargoyles.
Hold the Line is a great combat augment for this comp because of the amount of front line units it plays and lack of base AP values offered from traits.

2 Sets of carry items
Lots of flexibility in what to play frontline
How to Play:
Gameplan: This comp can be played from almost any spot, win or loss streak as long as you have Guinsoo’s for LeBlanc and a second set of carry items. Ideally you have an offensive Arbiter that allows LeBlanc to scale into the fight but it is not fully necessary if you can reach her BIS. There are a lot of variants to this comp, the 4 Vanguard version is the simplest to stabilize around but is by no means max cap.Stage 1-2: Play your strongest opener, ideally around a Guinsoo’s slam. If you don’t have a strong opener prioritize taking an econ augment and playing Primordians or Timebreakers for econ.
Stage 3: Continue to play into your streak in either direction and collecting LeBlanc and Karma core items.
Stage 4: Level on 4-2 for LeBlanc and Karma, focus on making 3 LeBlanc items if you have Guinsoo first. If you don’t have Guinsoo it is recommended to try to play around a different carry unless you have specifically a AS generating Arbiter.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 when possible and cap around legendaries. The board shown above is not max cap but will be stable for early stage 5.
Tips:
Picking the correct Arbiter is very skill testing for this comp. Try to plan out your items to compliment what you pick. For example, if you have an Archangel’s built AS Arbiters will be better than AP Arbiters.
Karma and Nami can’t primary carry, they do a lot of AoE damage but struggle to finish off targets on their own, prioritize LeBlanc’s items first.
Nami and Karma are interchangeable, they both utilize generic AP items decently. Prioritize playing Replicator for Nami.
The core traits to the board are 3 Shepherd with LB + Karma/Nami + 2 Arbiter. Your front line can be 5 costs or Mecha if necessary but these options are often more expensive and specific than 4 Vanguard.
3 Arbiter will often be overkill but if you need the raw stats on LeBlanc consider playing Zoe.

Conditions:
High HP and ability to reach level 9
Early Graves preferred
Infinity Edge Jhin
How to Play:
Gameplan: Fast 9 is rough this set as there is no 5 cost tank to stabilize your front line, meaning often times if you can’t fast 9 by 4-5 all the copies of front liners will be gone. Most of the time you will pivot into this board from a level 8 comp. If you don’t roll for a 2 star 4 cost tank, Jhin will not have enough time to close out the fight. Graves can help this comp cap very high but is not playable after 5-2, the earlier the better.Stage 1-2: Play a strong opener around strong AD slams, if you can’t win streak do not play this comp.
Stage 3: Keep up the tempo and win streak. If you fall behind look to default a different AD comp. It can’t be stressed enough this comp is very hard to play if you don’t have enough HP and econ to successfully find Jhin 2, Jhin 1 doesn’t do nearly enough damage.
Stage 4: If you can go 9 on 4-5, do so to find a 4 cost 2 star tank. The earlier you find Graves the better. If you have to roll on 8, look to carry Xayah or Corki and pivot to those respective comps.
Stage 5+: Go 9 if you haven’t already and roll for your board. The latest turn Graves is playable is 5-2. If you can’t find Graves add front line for Jhin as his damage is a little slow.
Tips:
Jhin’s damage is very high but spread out meaning he needs time to finish fights, prioritize having enough front line.
Graves and Bard provide the single target damage needed to close out fights so it is very important to have a duo carry with 3 items.
Graves Build path: Assault Frame > Melt Through > Grav Booster > Buckshot++. Only take 1 proc of Grav Boosters before taking all of the Buckshot upgrades. Assault Frame is currently over stated and his best initial choice.
Prioritize CC immunity on Graves.
Graves caps higher than Jhin and if you find him early enough it’s advised to prioritize him.
This comp can be pivoted in to from Corki variants as Corki and Jhin share the same itemization.

Graves: Edge of Night, Giant Slayer, Striker’sSterak’s, Titan’s, QSS
Rammus: Protector’s Vow/Mana generating Tank items
Bard: Archangel’s, Morello, Void Staff
Augments:
BIS: Bronze For Life
General: Econ > Items > Combat

Gameplan: This comp can serve 2 purposes, an engine to reach level 9, or a 3 cost reroll comp with win out potential as long as you have Uplink Drone. If you have Drone heavily consider this comp and slam Viktor items. Almost any AP slam is fine because anything suboptimal for Viktor can go on Nami. If you have to loss streak play timer breakers and plan to spike on 3-5 at level 7.
Stage 3: Continue to be strong if possible, level and roll on 3-5 if you are loss streaking. By this point you should be scouting and deciding if Viktor 3 is possible of not. If not look to set up for fast 9. The 2 main factors are how healthy you are and how cheaply you stabilize on 7 and 8.
Stage 4: Stay on 7 if you are rerolling if not, Roll on 4-2 at 8 for a board if you didn’t on 3-5. Viktor 2, Illaoi 2, Nami 1 and the supporting cast are very strong on this stage, specially if you managed to find Bronze for Life. If you can’t make it to 9 due to HP and also can’t hit Viktor 3 play for Nami 2 and to save as many placements as possible by winning most of stage 4 and early 5.
Stage 5+: Go 8/9 if you haven’t already and look for any 5 cost. This comps goal is to be strong on stage 4 so you should have lives to play with.
Tips:
Having 3 Item Viktor and Nami is an easy way to go 9 and also makes the pivot into Bard very easy.
It’s not advised to play this line if you don’t have an AP or Tank Psionic item.
If you have to stay on 8 commit to being strong from 4-2 on and top 4ing that way.
Viktor best itemization is pure damage.

Invader Zed Augment

How to Play:
Gameplan: The spots to play this comp are rare as this augment is only offered on 3-2. Only play this if you have a spot with strong tempo and think you can get to level 9. Zed is a traitless unit that needs BIS to be consistent. Since Zed is traitless the only way to reliably buff him is strong 5 cost aura effects. This comp also wants to see an early Graves as that is the highest capping duo carry. Any duo carry can work with Zed.Stage 1-2: You can’t plan for this comp on stage 1 or 2. You generally get to play this from a strong tempo opener. It’s not advisable to slam Zed items at this point. Make what you have as long as it win streaks you because this comp needs HP to get to 9. NOVA boards can reliably buff Zed and provide a strong opener.
Stage 3: Take Zed’s Augment on 3-2 and start looking for his items. Edge of Night and 1 Shojin are 100% necessary so if that’s not realistic do not click this.
Stage 4: Level on 4-2 and look for a 4 cost tank before they’re all out of the pool. You can be flexible here as Zed has no traits but TK is ideal as he synergizes with NOVA and can print you Zed 2. There are many duo carry options with Yi and Kindred being the easiest ones to play into at level 8. At 9 look to play Vex or Graves.
Stage 5+: Level to 9 and look for Zed 2 and 5 cost to buff your clones. Don’t play Graves after 5-2 unless you have a lot of HP.
Tips:
This comp is strong but very conditional. If you are low HP playing for Zed is very risky.
Zed’s clones inherit items in the same state as the creator’s, meaning if you have already used an item like Edge of Night the clone will not be able to activate its effect. This makes getting casts off as soon as possible the highest priority. If a clone hasn’t used Edge of Night any clones it spawns will also have Edge of Night so this isn’t based on the original Zed’s item state.
Do not build spell crit in this comp as Akali’s NOVA buff provides it.
Do not build Shred or Sunder as Aatrox’s NOVA buff provides it.

On Stage 3-1, at level 4, you can roll to 32g (most common), slow roll, or roll until you hit 3*.
Be flexible in when you roll, be willing to break econ intervals if you are close or need tempo. Ideally finish 1 3 star by 3-5.
All in on 4-1 if you haven’t hit already.
Conditions:
Stellar Combo Aatrox Hero Augment
BIS Items
How to Play:
Gameplan: Play this as you would a normal 1 cost reroll comp. Aatrox is a standard melee carry stat stick similar to Master Yi. Prioritize BIS Aatrox BIS, burn AP items on TF. TF 3 can rebuild your econ if you roll deep early stage 3.Stage 1-2: Hold every copy of Aatrox, TF, Caitlyn, Talon and Jax. If you have multiple upgrades its possible to win streak.
Stage 3: Roll aggressively to be strong on this stage. It should be pretty easy to 3 star at least 1 if not more 1 cost during this stage.
Stage 4: If you haven’t hit Aatrox 3, dig aggressively on 4-1. Be as strong as possible around your 3 stars during this stage. Chase Jax 3 if you have 6-7 copies, otherwise push for 5 NOVA.
Stage 5+: Push levels for 5 NOVA, if you don’t have access to it yet, 4 Bastion can be played in transition.
Tips:
Don’t make Shred or Sunder playing this comp as Aatrox’s NOVA buff offers it.
The best NOVA strike to take is Caitlyn’s as it provides 10% bonus damage. Aatrox’s NOVA strike doesn’t deal nearly enough damage.
Aatrox cycles through a variation of the same ability 3 times before resetting. His first cast deals damage to 1 target, the second becomes a cone that shreds flat armor, followed with a finishing slam that AoE knocks up.
The Medallion is the best Stargazer constellation for this comp.
Item Holder: Aatrox, TF, Caitlyn
Best Emblem/Spatula Holder: NOVA TF, NOVA Jax
Items:
Aatrox: Titan’s, Sterak’s, Bloodthirster
TF: Nashor’s, Archangel’s, Striker’sLeftover AP
Caitlyn: Rageblade, Kraken, DeathbladeLeftover AD
Jax: Generic Tank
Gods: Varus, Kayle
Augments:
BIS: Stellar Combo Aatrox Hero Augment
General: Hero > Reroll > Item > Econ > Combat
Not Special Tier: These comps require an augment and are not that great or bad. Only play from an incredible spot

How to Play:
Gameplan: Play this as a standard 1 cost reroll prioritizing Nasus, Leona and Teemo. Nasus is a scaling carry so roll aggressively for him on stage 3. The best condition to click this is when it would immediately give you a Nasus 2 so he can stack.Stage 1-2: Play your strongest opener around Nasus, Teemo +1 Vanguard. Play 3 Space Groove is possible. Do not play this comp from open as each time Nasus gets a kill with his spell it deals more damage permanently.
Stage 3: Roll deep on 3-1 to stabilize, at a minimum upgrade your entire board to 2 star. If you’re close to Nasus it’s ok to roll down to 10 to try to hit early. Continue rolling aggressively during this stage, if you lose here, you’ll likely lose out.
Stage 4: Roll for whatever you haven’t 3 starred on 4-1. Maintain tempo and keep stacking your Nasus.
Stage 5+: Level whenever possible for more Vanguards, 6 Vanguard is a huge spike as it grants DR when shielded.
Tips:
Nasus enters the groove on kill meaning he gets Space Groove’s AS and % healing buff almost immediately if you position him right. Prioritize being on the weakside of your opponents weakside.
If you fall behind tempo with this comp, you will remain behind so be willing to roll aggressively for an early Nasus 3.
Teemo 3 needs Guinsoo’s but the rest of his itemization is just generic AP.
Any arbiter that provides econ can be played early game.

Conditions:
Contract Killer Pyke Hero
Target-Lock Optics Psionic Item bumps this comp up a tier
Positioning Heavy
How to Play:
Gameplan: Pyke’s hero augment grants him a passive that gives you a 10% chance to farm a gold on any kill, meaning your early game needs to be strong. This comp becomes a lot better with Target-Lock Optics as its Pyke’s best item. Pyke Targets the lower HP target in a 2 Hex so always be on weakside frontline to farm maximum gold.Stage 1-2: Pyke is incredibly strong stage 2 and it should be easy to get multiple kills and start farming gold. If you happen to have IE Slam getting multiple resets is possible. The stronger you are the richer and easier the rest of the game will be.
Stage 3: Level to 6 on 3-2 and roll aggressively to be strong. Pyke’s chances of dropping gold on kill go up by star level so hitting Pyke 2 here is key. After Pyke 2 you can level to 7 so you can roll for Viktor 3, Yi and 4 Psionic.
Stage 4: Continue to roll for Pyke 3, Gragas 3 and Viktor 3 on level 7. Most 2 cost reroll comps stay on 6, but finding 4 Psionic on stage 4 is a lot of tempo.
Stage 5+: Level for supporting units after finding your 3 stars. Bruisers are really efficient if you have Biomatter Preserver on Gragas 3.
Tips:
Pyke’s hero augment grants him a passive that gives you a 10% chance to farm a gold on any kill, increased to up to 100% if Pyke is 3 starred and gets the last hit. Position on enemy weakside every fight to farm as much money as possible. This is very important early game to build an econ advantage.
Most 2 cost reroll comps stay on 7 but there is too much tempo to be found in 4 Psionic so going 7 for a Copy of Yi is key to a good stage 4.
You can check your Psionic item in your team planner if you are offered this augment on 2-1. Don’t play this if your Psionic is not good.

FAQ
How are compositions ranked?There are many factors, but the two strongest ones are how often they can be played and how strong they are when you get it. Think of it like frequency of being played combined with how well it can potentially do.
I also rank them based on how often the best players in the world play each comp (top 10 players in major regions)
Why isn’t XYZ Comp here?Probably not played enough, not strong enough, or maybe it hasn’t been discovered yet and will hopefully be added next week.
It’s also impossible to fit every single variation of every composition on a tier list, so expect variations of these comps to do well too.
I also add in different versions of different comps in the notes, so be sure to read through them! (For example, one synergy might have two different playstyles such as reroll or standard)
[Legendary Unit] carry is the best in the game, where is it?It is not reliable to have a 5 cost carry as a composition because you will not be able to get a 2* Legendary consistently. There may be metas where there are ‘Fast 9’ comps, but these often use any legendary they can get instead of a specific one.
What does Difficulty, Item Dependency, and Variance mean?Difficulty is how hard the composition is to play.  Difficulty does not factor into the strength or viability of the composition but serves as a factor for new players. 
Item dependency is how important specific items are to the composition. 
Variance is the approximate placement range of the composition.  For example, a consistent Top 4 composition has Low variance.  A composition that either places 1st or 8th has a High variance.
Does what composition I play matter?No. Playing TFT well matters a lot more
I can’t get these exact items every gameYou don’t need perfect items or exact items unless specified in the Requirements section. Most of the time you just need ‘playable’ items and not ‘best in slot’ (BIS)
You are wrong, XYZ comp should be in S tier and ABC player said this S tier comp sucksEveryone has different opinions. I try to take a data based approach by analyzing games from the best players in each region to combine all their opinions.
At the end of the day, comp doesn’t matter much compared to just playing TFT well (rolling, managing econ, positioning, etc). If you check out the best players, you will see that each player favors different compositions yet they are all very highly ranked.
When is this site updated?Every Friday
Where can I learn more?There are many resources and players to learn from. I suggest starting at my YouTube channel and this website.
Knowing how to get better at TFT is much more important than knowing what compositions to play. Knowing how to play Teamfight Tactics will help you no matter what patch it is.
Tier placement assumes strong play.  Refer to Difficulty metric before attempting to play.

### [Tour 5] Assistant Gemini :
Matrice de Décision Initiale (Stage 2-1) L'orientation de la partie se détermine par la convergence entre les composants initiaux, les unités naturelles (drops) et les conditions de plateau. Condition d'Ouverture Composants Prioritaires Composition Cible Décision / Déclencheur (Trigger) Constellation Favorable Arcs (Bows), Épées (Swords) Stargazer Xayah Constellation Serpent , Boar , ou Altar active. Obligation de forger Kraken Slayer et Red Buff . Tempo Meeple Épées, Arcs Gnar Printer Obtention de Gnar + 3 Meeples (ex: Poppy, Rammus) très tôt. HP élevés requis pour survivre à la phase d'impression. Augment / Psionic Épées, Gants Brawler Yi Item Psionique Malware Matrix / Target-Lock Optics ou Emblème (Marauder/Brawler). Nécessite Edge of Night . Tempo Primordian Épées, Gants Primordian Jinx 3 Primordians (ex: Briar, Rek'Sai, Bel'Veth) dès le 2-1. Nécessite de la pure AD ( Deathblade ) sur Jinx. Tanking / AP Pure Armures, Manteaux, Baguettes Mecha Défense parfaite slamable ( Gargoyle ) et AP sans mana ( Deathcap , Jeweled Gauntlet ) pour Asol. Priorités de Draft en Early Game (Stages 1 & 2) Pour maximiser l'économie et la flexibilité vers ces 5 compositions, le hold des unités doit suivre cette hiérarchie stricte : Unités à 1 PO : 2 Rogue (Talon, Gwen, Briar, Fizz) : Le meilleur trait d'early pour la mitigation d'aggro. Excellents porteurs d'items AD pour Xayah, Yi ou Gnar. Rek'Sai : Point de pivot central. Active Primordian (pour Jinx) et Brawler (pour Yi). Unités à 2 PO : Pyke : Excellent porteur pour Yi si l'item Psionique est AD. Jinx & Bel'Veth : À sécuriser immédiatement pour évaluer la viabilité de Primordian Jinx . Pantheon & Milio : Ligne de front générique, ouvre la voie vers Mecha ou les transitions AP. Unités à 3 PO : Kai'Sa : Synergise avec les Rogues et offre un mid-game à très haut tempo (4 Dark Star). Illaoi : Stabilisation brute de la frontline (utile pour temporiser Gnar ou Mecha). Arbre des Pivots ("Outs" de Secours) Si la composition ciblée est contestée (scouting) ou si la distribution des items (RNG) diverge, l'optimisation exige un pivot vers des structures partageant les mêmes ressources. 1. Plan A : Stargazer Xayah compromis Cause : Constellation défavorable (ex: Medallion ) ou manque d'Arcs (pas de Kraken Slayer ). Out 1 (AD Flex) : Corki Riven. Absorbe les items AD/Crit. Utilise l'infrastructure Meeple (si déjà en place) ou Fateweaver. Out 2 (Tempo Win Streak) : Vex Fast 9. Si la série de victoires est maintenue grâce aux slams d'early, poussez au niveau 9. Graves absorbera les items de Xayah. 2. Plan A : Gnar Printer compromis Cause : Saignement de PV trop important avant le niveau 8 (incapacité à imprimer en sécurité). Out 1 : Corki Riven. Gnar est déjà un Meeple et porte parfaitement les items de Corki (Guinsoo, IE). Out 2 : Brawler Yi. Si des items de survie ( Edge of Night ) ont été forgés, transférez le DPS mêlée sur Yi. 3. Plan A : Brawler Yi compromis Cause : Mauvais items Psioniques ou absence d'Emblèmes. Out 1 : Primordian Jinx / Reroll. Si le jeu fournit Akali et Bel'Veth mais refuse Yi, transférez le carry sur Jinx (nécessite d'être niveau 6/7). Out 2 : Vex Fast 9. Si le tempo est excellent, ignorez Yi et jouez la transition vers les légendaires (Fiora prendra les items mêlée). 4. Plan A : Mecha compromis Cause : Impossible de trouver Mighty Mech ou Asol, ou contestation sévère. Out 1 : Asol AP Flex (Variante Vanguard). Remplacez le Mech par 4 Vanguards. Sona, Karma ou Nami peuvent agir en carry secondaire AP. Out 2 : Vanguard Karma LeBlanc. Si les items AP génèrent du mana ( Shojin , Blue Buff ) - ce qui ruine Asol - pivotez sur Karma et LeBlanc. 5. Plan A : Primordian Jinx compromis Cause : Contestation sur Jinx, ou incapacité à frapper les 3 étoiles avant le stage 4-5. Out 1 : Brawler Yi. Le squelette est déjà en place (Bel'Veth, Akali, Rek'Sai). Poussez au niveau 8 et transférez les items AD vers Yi et Kindred.

### [Tour 7] Assistant Gemini :
L'incompréhension est logique : la mécanique de transition n'était pas assez explicite. Dans TFT, la construction d'un plateau (board) en début de partie (early game) ne se fait pas au hasard, elle repose sur l'optimisation des mots-clés (traits) partagés entre vos porteurs d'objets temporaires (item holders) et votre composition finale. Voici la cartographie systémique de vos ouvertures (openers), croisée avec la Tier List des unités pour maximiser la rentabilité de votre plateau dès le Stage 2. 1. Stargazer Xayah : L'ingénierie de l'Opener Sniper/Meeple Pour jouer Xayah, vous avez besoin d'une ligne de front solide et d'un porteur d'objets AD (dégâts physiques) capable d'utiliser les mêmes synergies. L'Opener optimal : Gnar (Tier B) est l'unité clé. Il possède les traits Sniper et Meeple. Il porte parfaitement Kraken Slayer et Red Buff en attendant Xayah. La Frontline : Pour accompagner Gnar, vous jouez naturellement Poppy (Tier B) et Rammus (Tier A) . Ils apportent la synergie Bastion pour encaisser les dégâts, et activent le trait 3 Meeple avec Gnar. La mécanique du Pivot (Out) : C'est exactement pour cette raison que Corki Riven est votre porte de sortie. Si au niveau 8, le jeu vous refuse Xayah (ou si la constellation Stargazer est mauvaise), vous avez déjà Rammus et Gnar sur le terrain. Il suffit de transférer les objets de Gnar sur Corki (qui est aussi un Meeple) pour rentabiliser l'infrastructure Meeple/Bastion que vous avez construite depuis le Stage 2. 2. Gnar Printer : La conservation agressive des PV Cette composition utilise le même squelette de départ que Xayah, mais l'objectif de fin de partie diverge : vous ne vendez pas Gnar, vous l'imprimez. L'Opener optimal : Gnar (Tier B) , Poppy (Tier B) , Rammus (Tier A) . Sécurisation du plateau (Tier List) : L'impression via le trait 7 Meeple va vous faire perdre beaucoup de points de vie au Stage 4. Pour compenser, votre Stage 2 doit être impénétrable. Intégrez Shen (Tier S) dès que possible. Avec un Top Moyen de 3.84, Shen Bastion/Bulwark va geler les dégâts adverses et garantir votre économie de PV. La mécanique du Pivot (Out) : Si vous saignez trop de PV avant d'atteindre 7 Meeple , vous ne pourrez pas imprimer. Vendez les Meeples inutiles et transférez l'équipement de Gnar sur Brawler Yi ou Vex Fast 9 , des compositions qui stabilisent immédiatement au niveau 8. 3. Brawler Yi : L'optimisation des Rogues et Primordians Master Yi est un carry de mêlée. Votre early game doit pouvoir porter des objets de survie ( Edge of Night ) et d'amplification de dégâts. L'Opener optimal : Gwen (Tier A) et Talon (Tier D) activent 2 Rogue , ce qui permet de dissiper l'aggro (mécanique vitale pour porter Edge of Night en early). Pyke (Tier C) est prioritaire si vous avez l'objet Psionic Target-Lock Optics . L'Unité charnière : Rek'Sai (Tier C) . Bien qu'elle soit statistiquement faible seule, elle relie la composition : elle active Brawler (pour Yi plus tard) et Primordian (pour générer de l'économie immédiate). La mécanique du Pivot (Out) : Vous associez Rek'Sai à Bel'Veth (Tier B) pour tenir le mid-game. Si Master Yi est introuvable au niveau 8, vous possédez déjà 2/3 des Primordians et des Marauders. Il est alors fluide de basculer l'équipement AD sur Primordian Jinx (si vous êtes niveau 7) ou de jouer autour de Bel'Veth. 4. Mecha : Le verrouillage de l'AP et de l'Armure Aurelion Sol (AP pur, sans génération de mana) et Mighty Mech (Tank pur) exigent une ouverture capable de rentabiliser ces objets bruts sans perdre de tempo. L'Opener optimal : Blitzcrank (Tier S) . C'est l'unité la plus contestée et la plus rentable du jeu (Top 3.92, 29.8% de fréquence). Posez vos objets défensifs ( Gargoyle's ) sur lui. Pour les objets AP, Lissandra (Tier C) ou Teemo (Tier A) feront l'affaire. L'Unité charnière : Pantheon (Tier B) . Il est Brawler (Frontline) et Replicator. La mécanique du Pivot (Out) : Si Mighty Mech n'apparaît pas dans la boutique, votre investissement sur Blitzcrank (Vanguard) est rentable : pivotez sur Asol AP Flex en jouant 4 Vanguards pour protéger Asol, ou remplacez Asol par Karma (Tier A) si vous avez accidentellement fabriqué un objet de mana. 5. Primordian Jinx : Le pari du tempo absolu Statistiquement, Jinx est une unité de Tier D (Top 5.03) . Jouer autour d'elle est mathématiquement une erreur, sauf si les conditions de synergie écrasent ses statistiques individuelles au Stage 2. L'Opener optimal : Vous ne pouvez jouer cette ligne que si le jeu vous donne Jinx (Tier D) , Bel'Veth (Tier B) et Rek'Sai (Tier C) très rapidement. C'est l'activation immédiate du trait 3 Primordian (génération de Swarmlings) qui compense la faiblesse native de Jinx. La mécanique du Pivot (Out) : Si la contestation est forte ou que Jinx 3* ne tombe pas, votre base est composée de Rek'Sai (Brawler) et Bel'Veth (Marauder). En surface : La bouée reste en position basse sous l'effet de la gravité, laissant les voies d'admission d'air ouvertes. ### [Tour 2] Utilisateur (19:16:15) :

### [Tour 2] Assistant Gemini :
La manœuvre de Valsalva sert à équilibrer la pression entre l'oreille moyenne et le milieu extérieur (l'air ou l'eau), afin d'éviter les douleurs et les lésions au niveau du tympan lorsque l'on descend en profondeur. Voici l'explication mécanique de son utilité : Le problème physique : Le gradient de pression Lorsque vous descendez sous l'eau, la pression hydrostatique augmente rapidement (elle double dès 10 mètres de profondeur). Cette pression pousse le tympan vers l'intérieur de l'oreille. L'oreille moyenne (derrière le tympan) est une cavité fermée contenant de l'air. Si la pression à l'intérieur de cette cavité reste inférieure à la pression extérieure, le tympan est étiré de force, ce qui provoque une douleur vive, puis un barotraumatisme (allant de la congestion de l'oreille jusqu'à la rupture du tympan). Le rôle de la manœuvre : Ouvrir les trompes d'Eustache La nature a prévu un canal de communication entre l'arrière-gorge et l'oreille moyenne : la trompe d'Eustache . Au repos, ce canal est collabé (fermé). La manœuvre de Valsalva consiste à : Se pincer le nez. Fermer la bouche. Expirer doucement comme si on voulait se moucher. Cette action augmente la pression de l'air dans les voies aériennes supérieures. L'air sous pression force l'ouverture des trompes d'Eustache et s'injecte directement dans l'oreille moyenne. La pression interne rééquilibre immédiatement la pression externe : le tympan reprend sa position neutre et la douleur disparaît. Pourquoi l'Easybreath bloque cette manœuvre ? Pour effectuer cette manœuvre, il est indispensable de bloquer mécaniquement les narines avec les doigts pour empêcher l'air de s'échapper par le nez. La visière rigide et intégrale de l'Easybreath rend le nez totalement inaccessible, ce qui interdit son exécution et limite donc structurellement l'utilisation du masque à la surface.

C'est le placage de masque. La solution normale : Avec un masque classique, on expire un filet d'air par le nez pour rajouter de la pression dans le masque et compenser l'écrasement. Avec les bouchons de nez : Votre nez étant obstrué en permanence, vous ne pouvez absolument pas injecter d'air dans le masque. ## Session `359693a517d0db8a` (2026-06-27 04:36:04)

### [Tour 1] Utilisateur (04:36:04) :
What's with the manwha/manhua slop? ( Especially the latter)

### [Tour 1] Assistant Gemini :
The explosion of repetitive, low-effort Manhwa and Manhua—often affectionately or derisively labeled as "slop"—comes down to a mix of hyper-industrialized production pipelines, platform algorithms, and monetization models optimized for rapid dopamine hits rather than artistic longevity. While both mediums suffer from mass production, Manhua (Chinese webcomics) often feels like a deeper offender than Manhwa (Korean webtoons) due to distinct systemic differences. 1. The Assembly Line Production Model Modern webcomics are rarely the product of a single passionate auteur. They are manufactured by massive corporate studios (e.g., Kakao Entertainment, Naver, or various Chinese studios) using a strict division of labor: One person adapts the script from a pre-existing web novel. Another handles the line art, while assistants use asset packs (like SketchUp or Aree) for backgrounds, horses, and buildings. Coloring and special effects are outsourced to speed specialists. Because these studios reuse the same 3D assets, fonts, and structural templates, hundreds of series end up with the exact same visual identity and structural pacing. 2. The Web Novel Ecosystem (The Root of Recycled Tropes) Most of this "slop" is not original material; it is a quick-turnaround adaptation of web novels. The Formula: Authors of web novels are paid based on daily word counts and immediate reader retention. To survive, they rely heavily on established, high-dopamine meta-tropes that require zero world-building. The Copy-Paste Genres: Manhwa: System/Gate regression, Tower climbing, Necromancy, Otome Isekai ("I became the villainess"). Manhua: Urban Cultivation, System-assisted face-slapping, "Betrayed but I have an OP grandpa/artifact." If a novel performs decently, a studio immediately options it for a comic adaptation to cash in before the trend shifts, resulting in a market flooded with identical premises. 3. Why Manhua Feels Notably Worse While Manhwa has polished its factory line to a high technical standard (dynamic lighting, clean line work, structured pacing), Manhua often feels significantly lower in quality due to specific market pressures in China: Extreme Chapter Delivery Rates Manhua production schedules are brutal. While a Manhwa creator typically releases one long, high-quality chapter a week, Manhua schedules often demand two to three updates per week . To maintain this cadence, studios drastically cut corners: The "Copy-Paste" Panel: Characters will have identical poses across multiple chapters, with only the background gradient changing. Fractured Pacing: Chapters are often incredibly short, ending abruptly mid-interaction because the storyboard was stretched thin to meet the multi-update weekly quota. The "Face-Slapping" Narrative Loop The structural core of the average urban or cultivation Manhua relies on Duanzi (short, punchy, immediate gratification loops). The narrative rarely focuses on long-term character arcs or cohesive world-building. Instead, it runs on a perpetual loop: An arrogant young master/rich businessman insults the main character (MC). The MC reveals their hidden, god-like identity, status, or power. The antagonist is humiliated ("face-slapped"). Repeat with a slightly more powerful antagonist in the next chapter. Because the Chinese digital comic market relies heavily on microtransactions for individual, short chapters via apps like Tencent Comics or Kuaikan, creators cannot afford slow-burn setups. If a chapter doesn't deliver immediate catharsis or a cliffhanger within 10 panels, readers drop it. Censorship Constraints Chinese content regulation (NRTA) strictly monitors themes involving ghosts, heavy gore, explicit sexuality, and political subversion. Traditional, complex subversion or dark fantasy elements are difficult to clear. Cultivation loops, historical romance, and urban power fantasies are safe, easily approved templates that guarantee a return on investment without regulatory risk. The Silver Lining The "slop" exists because it acts as predictable, low-effort comfort food that performs incredibly well on algorithmic feeds. However, the sheer volume of mass-produced titles means that when a studio does invest in high-tier adaptation teams, or when an original creator manages to break through the studio system, the contrast is stark. Thick layers of formulaic titles make the genuinely well-structured, meta-analytical, or visually distinct works stand out all the more.

The "Power Inflation" Trap: Zero Conceptual Depth In well-structured progression systems, power scaling is qualitative. A character learns a technique, and its utility scales with their understanding, tactical application, or creative synergy with other skills. In standard Manhua, power scaling is strictly quantitative and nominal . A technique isn't valuable because it's mechanically interesting; it's valuable because it belongs to a higher tier (e.g., Earth Grade vs. Heaven Grade ). The moment the main character breaches the next micro-realm or moves to a higher plane (the classic "new map" trope), the baseline changes. If the enemies in the new zone have a higher base defense stat than the maximum output of the previous zone's ultimate technique, that technique is instantly rendered mathematically obsolete. Because there is no deep mechanical interaction within the power system—only arbitrary numerical superiority—techniques are treated like disposable gear in an MMO rather than a core part of the character's identity. 2. The Micro-Chapter Dilemma The pacing loop feels incredibly short because of how content is parceled out. [ Manga ] — 18-20 dense pages weekly -> Slow burn, spatial setup, internal monologue. [ Manhwa ] — ~60 vertical panels weekly -> Linear progression, dynamic action choreography. [ Manhua ] — ~15-20 vertical panels 2-3x weekly -> Pure stimulus, zero breathing room. When a chapter only contains enough space for two exchanges of dialogue and a single energy blast, a creator cannot spend 5 chapters establishing the weight, cost, or mastery of a new ability. If Yang Kai spends 10 chapters training a technique, that represents two to three weeks of real-world release time where "nothing happens" according to the microtransaction-driven audience. To prevent reader churn, the acquisition must be immediate, the demonstration must happen in the next panel, and the narrative must sprint to the next conflict. 3. The "Next Map, Same Map" Structural Loop Manhua production is heavily reliant on web novel structures designed to run for thousands of chapters (e.g., Martial Peak ’s novel is over 6,000 chapters). To sustain this length without actual character development, the authors rely on fractal storytelling : [Start Zone] -> MC is trash -> MC finds artifact -> MC beats local Young Master -> MC dominates zone. | [Ascension to Next Zone] -> MC's power is reset to "trash" relative to locals -> Old techniques obsolete. | [New Zone] -> MC finds new technique -> MC beats new Young Master -> MC dominates zone. Because the structural loop itself is so short and rigid, the abilities must be disposable. If a technique acquired in the lower realm remained viable in the higher realm, it would disrupt the formulaic tension required to kickstart the next "face-slap" cycle. The narrative requires the character to constantly feel like they are starting from scratch against new arrogant elites, forcing a perpetual cycle of short-lived power-ups. Manhwa certainly isn't immune to rapid scaling (especially within the "System/Necromancy" genres), but it generally respects its own structural rules for longer stretches. A signature skill or an established narrative thread in a mid-tier Manhwa usually has enough structural support to last a few arcs. In contrast, the hyper-accelerated Manhua model turns progression into a treadmill running at maximum speed: you get the hit of adrenaline from the breakthrough, but the narrative terrain moves so fast underneath the character that the milestone is trivialized before the reader can even register its impact.

### [Tour 1] Assistant Gemini :
Les smartphones introduisent une latence réseau (overhead) variable et manquent de retour haptique, ce qui fausse la compétition lors d'un blind test. Pour obtenir une rigueur absolue sur le temps de réaction, il est impératif d'utiliser un système doté d'un verrouillage matériel ( hardware lockout ) ou d'un polling USB ultra-rapide. Voici trois solutions viables, classées de la plus accessible à la plus technique. 1. Le détournement de matériel : Les manettes "Buzz!" (PlayStation) C'est la solution la plus fiable à bas coût. Les buzzers filaires (ou sans fil avec dongle USB) des anciens jeux Buzz! sur PS2/PS3 sont d'excellents périphériques. Fonctionnement : Ils se connectent en USB et sont reconnus nativement par Windows comme des contrôleurs HID (Human Interface Device). Avantage technique : Le délai de transmission est extrêmement faible (celui de l'USB standard). Intégration : Il suffit d'utiliser un logiciel de quiz compatible sur PC ou de coder un petit script pour capturer les entrées. Le gros bouton rouge est très résistant aux frappes intenses. 2. Le système RF autonome : Les kits d'animation professionnels Si l'objectif est de s'affranchir totalement du PC pour la gestion des priorités, il existe des kits de buzzers sans fil (fréquence radio) utilisés par les animateurs. Fonctionnement : Un kit comprend plusieurs buzzers satellites et une télécommande ou console maître. Avantage technique : Le verrouillage est géré au niveau de la carte mère du kit. Dès qu'un signal RF est reçu, le système bloque les autres signaux et allume le buzzer gagnant. Il n'y a pas de problème de latence logicielle, le traitement est purement électronique. Inconvénient : Ne s'interface pas facilement avec un ordinateur pour automatiser les scores ou la lecture de la musique. 3. L'approche Ingénierie / DIY : Boutons d'Arcade et Serveur Local Pour un contrôle total sur l'environnement de jeu et la gestion des médias, la création d'un système d'acquisition sur mesure est la solution la plus aboutie. Matériel : Des boutons d'arcade (type Sanwa) couplés à des cartes Zero Delay Arcade USB (pour du filaire) ou à des microcontrôleurs type ESP32 (pour du sans fil). Architecture : Les inputs physiques envoient le signal à la machine maître. Un serveur local (ex: Node.js) écoute ces entrées. Pour une version sans fil via ESP32, l'utilisation de WebSockets garantit une transmission des événements de l'ordre de la milliseconde, sans passer par le cloud. Avantage technique : Ce type d'architecture permet de lier la logique de lockout à une interface front-end (ex: React) pour gérer la diffusion des musiques et l'affichage des scores en temps réel, le tout réparti et optimisé sur une configuration multi-écrans. Préfères-tu t'orienter vers un système de verrouillage purement matériel (indépendant) ou vers une solution interfacée avec ton PC pour centraliser la musique et l'affichage des scores ?

Il est tout à fait possible de contourner les kits professionnels à 150 € en assemblant soi-même une solution avec des composants d'arcade. C'est d'ailleurs la meilleure approche pour avoir un système robuste, évolutif et à bas coût (compte entre 30 € et 50 € pour 4 joueurs). Puisque tu as des bases techniques solides, voici comment monter un système de buzzers ultra-réactifs sans te ruiner. Le kit DIY idéal : L'encodeur "Zero Delay" + Boutons Dôme Au lieu d'acheter un système tout fait, on utilise les pièces destinées à fabriquer des bornes d'arcade. Le matériel à sourcer (sur Amazon ou AliExpress) : Des boutons "Dôme" d'arcade (60 mm ou 100 mm) : Ce sont les gros boutons ronds typiques des jeux télévisés. Certains intègrent des LED (5V ou 12V). Une (ou plusieurs) carte(s) "Zero Delay USB Encoder" : C'est le cœur du système. Cette petite carte électronique (souvent vendue moins de 10 €) permet de brancher des boutons d'arcade directement dessus avec des câbles Dupont fournis. Câblage : Les kits "Zero Delay" sont fournis avec les câbles. Il n'y a aucune soudure à faire , tout se clipse. Remarque : La carte USB est reconnue nativement par Windows comme une manette de jeu ou un clavier. Chaque bouton pressé envoie une commande (Bouton 1, Bouton 2, etc.) via l'USB avec un polling rate très élevé, supprimant le problème de latence. La gestion du "Lockout" (Le verrouillage) Dans cette configuration DIY, le matériel se contente d'envoyer l'information "Le joueur 3 a appuyé". C'est le logiciel sur ton PC qui doit gérer le lockout (prendre le premier signal, bloquer les autres, et lancer une animation). Pour cela, tu as deux options : 1. Utiliser un logiciel de Blind Test existant Il existe des logiciels conçus exactement pour ce cas de figure, capables de mapper des touches de clavier ou de manettes USB : iZiMiX : Un logiciel français très connu pour l'animation de blind tests. Il gère le lockout, l'attribution des points et l'affichage sur un second écran. Buzzz : Disponible sur le Microsoft Store, très basique mais efficace pour afficher qui a buzzé en premier. Easy Quiz / Quiz Pro : D'autres alternatives anglophones qui détectent les inputs clavier (touches 1, 2, 3, 4...). Si tu utilises des cartes Zero Delay, tu peux utiliser un petit utilitaire comme JoyToKey pour transformer l'appui du bouton d'arcade en touche de clavier. 2. Le développer toi-même (L'approche Dev) Puisque tu travailles avec des technos web (React, Node, etc.), tu peux coder ton propre système en quelques heures : Un front-end (React/Astro) qui écoute les événements keydown ou l'API Gamepad. Une logique métier ultra simple : if (isLocked) return; isLocked = true; declareWinner(playerId); . Tu peux y intégrer tes playlists Spotify ou des fichiers MP3 locaux, et afficher les scores et animations sur ton setup multi-écrans. C'est la solution ultime pour avoir exactement les règles et l'interface que tu souhaites. Alternative sans montage : Les pédales/boutons USB programmables Si tu ne veux pas t'embêter à brancher des fils sur une carte Zero Delay, tu peux acheter des "Boutons USB programmables" (parfois vendus comme pédales d'ordinateur ou boutons d'urgence industriels). Ils coûtent environ 10-15 € pièce. Tu les branches, tu utilises leur logiciel pour dire "Ce bouton correspond à la touche 'A' du clavier". Tu branches tes 4 boutons sur un Hub USB. Tu utilises ensuite un logiciel (ou ton propre code) pour gérer la touche A, B, C ou D. L'approche avec la carte "Zero Delay" reste la plus économique et offre les boutons les plus larges et les plus satisfaisants à frapper (les fameux dômes de 100 mm).
